newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end sharply lower in all months.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end sharply lower in all months.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed sharply lower on Thursday, with the September and the November contract down by the daily 500 yen limit on speculative selling from local investors, traders said.
The benchmark May 1998 contract ended down 380 yen at 16,020 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 71,591 lots.
The Chicago market's price plunge overnight and the yen's strong tone against the dollar triggered active selling throughout the day, traders said.
"Market players are sensitive to any bearish factor at the moment," a brokerage house trader said.

On CBOT Project A, the spot May corn contract was traded at $2.98 bushel at 0745 GMT, up from $2.97-1/4 at Wednesday's close. Spot May CBOT soybean futures were traded at $8.32-1/4 per bushel on the overnight trading system, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
